others.route: Work permit (Ministry of Labour and Human Welfare)

note: Eritrea: non-nationals may not work in Eritrea without a valid work permit issued under the Ministry's guidelines, showing the type of work and the length of employment, the Ministry being that of Labour and Human Welfare (Labour Proclamation No. 118/2001, Gazette of Eritrean Laws vol. 10 no. 5, 15 November 2001, arts. 2(33) and 8). Read by eye in the scanned Gazette FAOLEX holds (its text layer is a poor OCR, so the words are quoted as printed rather than checked against it). The regulations on issuing work permits to non-nationals (Legal Notice No. 80/2003) and the registration of foreigners (Proclamation No. 127/2002) weren't reached (UNHCR's Refworld archive puts this client behind a browser check), and no amendment to art. 8 was found. No performers' route and no days without the permit are named.

sources.title: Labour Proclamation of Eritrea, No. 118/2001 (Gazette of Eritrean Laws, vol. 10 no. 5, 15 November 2001), arts. 2(33) and 8 (FAOLEX scan)
sources.said: Non-nationals may not work in Eritrea without a valid work permit issued in accordance with guidelines issued by the Ministry. ... "Minister" and "Ministry" means the Minister and Ministry of Labour and Human Welfare, respectively.
